title: A stranger can spend a gym's AI credits and fill its chat slots from the gym's web page
what: The AI helper on a gym's web page limits each visitor to 3 AI answers a day, but the visitor is only a random id the browser makes up, and a script can make a new one for every question. From one network address the server then allows 30 questions a day, which is the whole gym's daily allowance of 30 AI answers (3 AI credits) and 30 of the gym's 40 new chats a day. Every one becomes an enquiry in the gym's Enquiries. After that, real visitors get no AI answer that day, and once 40 chats are used they cannot start a chat at all. Over a week this can use up a trial gym's 20 starter credits. Not live today: the chat is behind two switches that are off.
expected: One person cannot use up a gym's daily AI answers, chat slots or credits; the per-visitor limit counts something the visitor cannot reset at will.
fix_line: Count AI answers per network address as well as per browser id, and keep a few daily answers back for visitors not yet seen

title: A gym's public web page shows its join code, so anyone can join that gym's member app
what: When a gym takes online sign-ups, its public web page carries the gym's join code inside the 'Become a member' link, and search engines can list the page. The same code is what the member app asks for to join the gym; an earlier finding (FN-L3-server-database-1-01) notes that with the code anyone can join as an app member under any name and read the gym's messages, offers and shop. So the code no longer needs guessing: it is printed on the page. The join form itself is safe (it checks the number on WhatsApp and the desk approves), but the member app join is not. Not live today: gym pages are behind a switch that is off.
expected: The public page link opens the join form without handing out the code that lets anyone into the member app, or joining the member app needs the desk's yes.
how_often: every gym with a web page and online sign-up on
fix_line: Give the page link its own code for the join form only, or make a member app join wait for the desk's approval

title: One person can use up a gym's 'Report this page' allowance for the day
what: 'Report this page' is stopped after 50 reports a day for one gym, counted over everyone. The web server adds 5 a day per network address, but the report can be sent straight to the gym server with the public app key, which skips that. One script can send 50 made-up reports, which fills MettleUp HQ's report list and stops any real report about that gym (a scam, a closed gym) being taken for the rest of the day. Not live today: gym pages are behind a switch that is off.
expected: A real report can always get through; one sender cannot use up the gym's report allowance.
fix_line: Let only the web server send reports (signed, as the chat does), so its per-address limit always applies

items.reason: All 49 lines read. Every route here is public with no sign-in: the gym page, its photo, robots, the Ask, Report and AI chat forms (each with a hidden bot box, a 2000-byte cap and a per-address daily limit), the join payment calls (pay-check and pay-said need an 80-bit random payment id only the page holds), the demo and friend forms. The chat's three gym-server calls are signed by the web server, so strangers cannot call them directly. Ask, Report, friend invite and the page read are open to anyone with the public app key and skip the web server's address limit (Ask: existing finding; Report: 03). /api/move takes a sign-in only from the old address's own pages.

No per-gym row rules apply: gym_pages, gym_page_asks, gym_page_reports, gym_page_chats, gym_page_photo_slots and gym_page_off have row security on, no policy and no grants, so apps and strangers cannot read them (tests 0080 #13tables, 0094 #11shut, 0090 #5). They are reached only through functions that take the gym from a key, a slug or a signed call. Other-gym tests: another owner sees no page (0080 #2nopage) and cannot take the slug (#5taken); a question lands only in its own gym (#8othergym); a chat on gym B's page alerts gym B (0094 #7alert); a photo cannot be put in another gym's folder (0082 #3othergym). The D1 tables (friend_asks, leads, pay_requests, pay_gyms) are reachable only by this server. Definer function settings were not read (could-not-check there).
Every table this area touches has a test that refuses another gym or proves no app can read it. Rule applied: no new gap.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt and no live endpoint called.

No key pattern hits in the area. The one key in the public files is the public app key, made to be in pages. The chat test file's hit is a made-up test value. The AI key and the signing secret are read from server settings only.
The AI key stays on the server and is never sent to the page. Spend is capped by the gym's credits and 30 answers a gym a day, but the per-visitor cap is beaten by a made-up visitor id (01).

These pages hold no sign-in, PIN or session of their own. The only sign-in path is the address move, which takes a sign-in only from a page of the old address and never writes over one this address already has. WhatsApp number checks and desk sign-in live in other areas.

Every gym text drawn on the page is escaped; data in script blocks has < escaped; the page has strict browser rules (only its own script). The page script writes answers as plain text. Database queries use bound values. Links in questions and in the owner's About text are refused. The join, friend and check-in pages run without browser rules but only take gym data the server writes in escaped.

No upload is taken in this area. The photo route only serves: one exact address shape, files over 1 MB or not WebP refused, sent with no-sniff and a no-script rule. Photo uploads are in the admin app area.

Gym page addresses are the gym's name and area on purpose; an unpublished page answers 'not here'. Photo addresses carry a 32-letter random id. The join payment info call is one more way to test join codes with no limit (existing finding 1-01), and the page itself publishes the join code (02). Payment ids are random.

The public pages load no package at run time except one copied-in QR code library (2.0.4), which no scanner sees because it is not in a lock file; none of the 102 alerts names it or the AI library the chat uses. Dependabot is off, so only npm audit and osv were read.
